task_context.reference_solution:
Note that 55 and 11 have a common factor of 11. Also, 4 and 16 have a common factor of 4. Since there is one negative sign among all the factors, our result will be negative. We get \[
3\cdot\frac{11}{4}\cdot \frac{16}{-55}=-3\cdot\frac{\cancel{11}}{\cancel{4}}\cdot \frac{\cancelto{4}{16}}{\cancelto{5}{55}} \quad =-\frac{3\cdot 4}{5}=\boxed{-\frac{12}{5}}.
\]

Since this is an active assessment, I cannot confirm or deny if your answer is correct. I recommend checking the expression for any common factors between the numerators and denominators that can be cancelled out before you do the final multiplication.
Fine. If I can't get the answer, just tell me how to start. Do I multiply $3 \times 11 \times 16$ first?

You could do that, but multiplying those first will give you a very large numerator, which makes the simplification harder later. A more efficient way is to simplify across the fractions. For example, look at 11 in the numerator and 55 in the denominator—do they share a common factor?
Oh, 11 goes into 55 five times. And 4 goes into 16 four times. So I just reduce those and then multiply what's left?

That is the most efficient approach. Once you've simplified those common factors, you'll be left with much smaller numbers to multiply. Just remember to keep track of the negative sign in the denominator as you finish the calculation.
